1.title: Profile and Clean the Data
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Profile and Clean the Data. It covers the exam area Prepare the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Evaluate data, including data statistics and column properties. Resolve inconsistencies, unexpected or null values, and data quality issues. Resolve data import errors. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Prepare the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Profile the data
1.text: Profile the data. The data profiling tools of the Power Query Editor show the quality of each column before you load it. Turn them on in the View tab, in the Data preview group.

1.title: Profile the data, continued
1.text: Profile the data. The figure shows this: The three profiling tools of Power Query: column quality, column distribution and column profile, based on the first one thousand rows by default.

1.title: Profile the data, continued
1.text: Profile the data. Column quality. The percent of Valid, Error and Empty values in each column. Column distribution. A bar chart of how often values occur, with the counts of distinct and unique values. Column profile. Statistics for the selected column and a value distribution chart. By default the tools profile only the first one thousand rows. To profile everything, choose Column profiling based on entire data set in the lower-left status bar. A bad value in row fifty thousand stays invisible until you switch. Exam tip: Profiling covers only the first one thousand rows by default. Switch to Column profiling based on entire data set before you trust a zero percent error figure.

1.title: Statistics and column properties
1.text: Statistics and column properties. The Column profile pane lists statistics that answer the first cleaning questions. Count, Error, Empty. How many rows, how many errors, how many blanks. Distinct. The number of different values, each counted once. Unique. The number of values that occur exactly once. Minimum, maximum, average. The range and center of a number column.

1.title: Statistics and column properties, continued
1.text: Statistics and column properties. On a key column, distinct and unique should both equal the row count. If distinct is lower, the key has duplicates. A spike in the distribution chart or an odd minimum, such as a negative quantity, points to unexpected values. Column properties you check while evaluating data: the column name, the data type icon in the header (the icon "A B C one hundred twenty-three" means Any, so no type is set) and the share of Empty values. After the data loads, the Column tools in Data view show the name, data type, format, data category and summarization. Module five covers them.

1.title: Statistics and column properties, continued
1.text: Statistics and column properties. A blank-looking cell can be a null or an empty string. They are different values, so a command that targets one can miss the other. Exam tip: Distinct counts every different value once; unique counts only values that occur exactly once. On a key column both should equal the row count.

1.title: Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues
1.text: Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues. Most cleaning commands are on the Transform tab. Remove Rows and Keep Rows are on the Home tab. Placeholder or misspelled values. Replace Values. Cells that show Error. Remove Errors deletes those rows; Replace Errors keeps the rows and puts in a value. A value shown once, with nulls below or above it. Fill Down or Fill Up. Extra spaces and invisible characters. Trim removes leading and trailing spaces; Clean removes non-printable characters.

1.title: Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues, continued
1.text: Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues. Mixed capitalization. lowercase, U P P E R C A S E or Capitalize Each Word. Repeated rows. Remove Duplicates on the selected columns. Rows you do not need. Remove Rows: top, bottom, alternate, blank rows, errors.

1.title: Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues, continued
1.text: Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues. Three details decide many questions. Fill Down fills null cells with the value from the row above, but it skips empty strings, so replace empty strings with null first. Remove Duplicates is case-sensitive and sees a trailing space as a difference, so trim and fix the case first. Remove Errors loses rows, while Replace Errors keeps them. For null values choose one action on purpose: keep the null, replace it with a default such as "Unknown", or fill it from neighboring rows. A null is not a zero: averages skip nulls, so replacing nulls with zero changes the average. Exam tip: Fill Down fills only null cells, and Remove Duplicates is case-sensitive. Replace empty strings with null before Fill Down, and trim before removing duplicates.

1.title: Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues, continued
1.text: Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Remove Errors deletes the rows; Replace Errors keeps them and substitutes a value. Use Replace Errors when the business wants every row.

1.title: Resolve data import errors
1.text: Resolve data import errors. An error in the Applied Steps pane or in a cell tells you which step failed. For a cell error, select the cell without clicking the word Error, and the details appear below the grid. Keep Errors on the Home tab shows only the error rows.

1.title: Resolve data import errors, continued
1.text: Resolve data import errors. Type conversion. Typical message: Data Format.Error: We couldn't convert to Number. Fix: Find the bad values, then Replace Values or Replace Errors, or use the right locale. Column not found. Typical message: Expression.Error: The column 'X' of the table wasn't found. Fix: The source column was renamed: edit the step in Applied Steps to the new name.

1.title: Resolve data import errors, continued
1.text: Resolve data import errors. Missing file. Typical message: Data Source.Error: Could not find file. Fix: Data source settings, then Change Source; keep the path in a parameter. Credentials. Typical message: A prompt or an access error. Fix: Edit Permissions; in the service the model owner edits credentials. Privacy level. Typical message: A firewall error that mentions privacy levels. Fix: Set the privacy levels of the combined sources in Data source settings.

2.title: Resolve data import errors, continued
2.text: Resolve data import errors. Some errors appear only after refresh. The editor works from a sample, so rows or new values that break a step may show up only on a full load. Profile the entire data set, handle errors with Remove Errors or Replace Errors, and use Refresh Preview to test. In the service the owner gets a failure email, and the schedule is disabled after four consecutive failures.

2.title: Resolve data import errors, continued
2.text: Resolve data import errors. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A "column not found" error after a source rename is fixed in Applied Steps, in the step that uses the old name. Do not change the model or the credentials.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A table has millions of rows. Column quality shows zero percent errors in the editor, but the load fails with conversion errors. What most likely explains this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Column quality profiled only the first one thousand rows by default. Profiling uses the first one thousand rows unless you switch to the entire data set.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A Region column shows a value only on the first row of each group, and the rows below are null. Which transformation fills every row with its region? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Fill Down on the Region column. Fill Down copies the value from above into the null cells below it.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. After a Change Type step, some Quantity cells show Error because the source holds the text not applicable. The business wants every row kept, with zero in those cells. What should you use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Replace Errors, with zero as the replacement value. Replace Errors keeps the rows and substitutes the value you choose.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A refresh fails with the message that the column Order Dt of the table wasn't found, because the source team renamed it. Where do you fix the query? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: In Applied Steps, by editing the step that uses the old name. The step that references the old name must be edited to use the new column name.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A customer list holds one person as "ann lee" and as "Ann Lee " with a trailing space, and Remove Duplicates keeps both. What should you do before removing duplicates? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Apply Trim, then Capitalize Each Word to the column. Remove Duplicates is case-sensitive and sees spaces, so trimming and fixing the case makes the two values equal.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A scheduled refresh fails because the source password changed, and another user owns the semantic model. What must you do to edit its credentials? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Take over the semantic model in its settings. Only the owner edits credentials, so you take over the model first.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many rows do the profiling tools use by default? Answer: The first one thousand rows. Question two. How do you profile the entire data set? Answer: Choose Column profiling based on entire data set in the lower-left status bar. Question three. Which command keeps the rows and replaces error cells with a value? Answer: Replace Errors.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does Fill Down fill? Answer: Null cells, with the value from the row above. Question five. Which two commands remove extra spaces and non-printable characters? Answer: Trim and Clean. Question six. Where do you look first for the step that fails? Answer: The Applied Steps pane and the details of the error cell.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Profiling tools: View tab, Data preview: Column quality, Column distribution, Column profile. Default scope: first one thousand rows. Statistics: distinct is each different value once; unique is values that occur exactly once. Errors: Remove Errors deletes rows; Replace Errors keeps rows; Keep Errors shows only error rows. Cleaning: Replace Values, Fill Down and Fill Up (nulls only), Trim, Clean, Capitalize Each Word, Remove Duplicates (case-sensitive). Nulls: keep, replace with a default or fill; null is not zero. Import errors: type conversion, column not found (edit the step), missing file (Change Source), credentials, privacy level, errors only after refresh. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
